FORE W 0 R D

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 November 1976, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council,

0.2 Dalapon-sodium is a selective contact herbicide, translocated from foliage to roots. I t is used for the control of annual and perinnial grasses.
0.3 Dalapon-sodium is the common name approved by the Weed Science Society of America for sodium 2, 2-dichloropropionate. The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of dalapon-sodium arc as indicated below:
Empirical formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass

C aH aC1 2NaO a

CH aCCI 2.C0 2Na

165

0.4 In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable.

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall he founded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling
and test for dalapon-sodium, technical.

It shall be free from extraneous Impurities and added modifying agents. 2.2 The material shall also comply with the requirements specified in Table 1.

3. PACKING AND MARKING
3.1 Paekmg - The material shall be packed in clean and dry containers made of fibre board or mild steel or tin-plate lined with polyethylene liner of thickness not less than 0'062 mm. The container shall also comply with the general requirements specified in 2 of IS : 8190 (Part I )-1976*.

3.2 Marldng - The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information in addition to the provisions required under the Insecticides Act and Rules: a) Name of the material, the manufacturer, b) Name c) Date ormanufacture, d) Batch number, e) Net mass of contents, f) Active ingredient content percent ( mlm ), and

g) The minimum cautionary notice worded 'as under: 'DANGER. KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. KEEP AWAY }4'ROM FOODSTUFFS AND ANIMAL FEEDS. WASH HANDS THOROUGHLY WI"fH SOAP AND WATER A}4"fER HANDLING.' 3.2.1 The container nlay also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark.
NOTE - The use of the lSI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The lSI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by the produce-r. lSI marked products are also continuously checked by lSI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the lSI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standard.' Institution.

4. SAMPLING
4.1 Representative samples of the material shall he drawn as prescribed in 'Indian Standard methods for sampling of pesticides and their formulations' ( under preparation ). .
NOTE - Until the standard under preparation is published the matter shall be a. agreed between the concerned parties.

5. TESTS
5.1 Tests shall be carried out by appropriate methods as referred to in col 4 of Table 1. 5.2 Q,uality or Reagents - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water (see IS : 1070-1960� ) shall be employed in the tests.
NOTE - , Pure chemicals t shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

A

[Table 1, Item (i)]
DETERMINATION OF DALAPON-50DIUM CONTENT

A.o.GENERAL
1\-0.1 For the determination of active ingredient in dalapon-sodium two methods have been prescribed. However, in case of dispute, the infrared spectrophotometric method shall be considered as reference method. A-I. INFRARED SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC METHOD
A-1.0 Priaeiple - The sodium salt is converted to the corresponding acid which is extracted into carbon disulphide. The absorbance of the extract is compared to that of the absorbance of an extract of a standard by infrared spectrophotometer.

A-I.I Apparat.8 A-I.I.I Infrared Spectrophotometer - capable of recording in the region of
7 to 16 microns, with the slit width, gain and response time and scanning speed adjustable to produce a satisfactory signal-to-noise ratio and adequate resolution under the conditions of test.

A-l.1.2 Absorption Cells - scaled absorption cells, having an internal light path of I �0 mm. A-I.2 Reagent. A-l.2.1 Carbon Disulphide - analytical reagent grade. A-l.2.2 Sulphuric Acid - 25 percent ( vlv). A-l.2.3 Standard 2, 2-Dickloropropionic Acid� A-l.2.4 Sodium Chloride - analytical reagent grade.

A-I.3 Procedure A-I.3.1 Calibration
A-I.S.t.1 Weigh accurately 370 mg of standard 2, 2-dichloropropionic acid in a 50-ml volumetric flask, dissolve in carbon disulphide and dilute to the mark.
-Available OD requcst from Dow Chemical, New Delhi.

6

IS I 8267 � 1976

A-I.3.1.2 Fill the absorption cell with carbon disulphide. Adjust the spectrophotometer to the optimum instrument settings with respect to gain, slit width, response, speed and drum drive. Make scan with carbon disulphide in the cell over the wavelength region of 7 to 16 microns.
A-l.3.1.3 Turn the wavelength scale back to its original setting. Fill the cell with solution ( see A-l.3.1.1). Make a scan in the wavelength region of 1 to 16 microns, with the same setting as previously used (see A-I.3.1.2 ).

A-l.3.1.4 With the base line drawn from 8-6 to 9�8 microns, measure the absorbance of the solution at 8-9 micron. A-l.3.2 Estimation of Active Ingredient in the Malerial- Weigh accurately 500 mg of the sample in a 50-rol volumetric flask, add 1 ml of sulphuric acid and mix. Add 50 ml of carbon disulphide and 2 g of sodium chloride. Shake to dissolve. A-l.3.2.1 Make a scan of carbon disulphide and the carbon disulphide solution of the material (Stt A-l.3.2) as prescribed under A-I.3.1.2 and A-l.3.1.3 using the same cell and setting, Measure the absorbance as prescribed in A-l.3.1.4_ A-l.4 Calculation.

A-I.6 IdeDtiSeatioD - Compare the entire spectrum (7-16 micron) of the sample with that of standard to ascertain the identity. The sample may show impurity bands of 2, 2-chloropropionic acid at 8-3 and 10-1 microns; 2, 2,3-trichloropropion!c acid at 1~-05 :,nd 13�3 nlic~ol18; dichloroacetic acid at 12�2 micron and trichloroacetic acid at 12-1 micron.

A-2. TITRIMETRIC METHOD
A-2.0 Prmeiple - The complex formed by reacting dalapon-sodium, mercuric and cupric nitrates is filtered off, decomposed with aqueous potassium iodide and the potassium hydroxide thus formed is titrated with standard acid. A-2.1 Apparatus
A-2.1.1 Conical Flasks - 250-ml capacity, with ground joint. A-2.1.2 RtJluxCondenser A-2.1.3 Sintered Glass Crucible - 60-ml capacity. A-2.1.4 Water Bath

A-2.2 Reagents A-2.2.1 Cupric Mercuric Nitrate Solution - prepared by dissolving 100-0 g of yellow mercuric oxide and 60�0 g of cupric nitrate [ Cu (NO. )1_3H.O ] in nitric acid in a l-Iitre volumetric flask. Make up the volume with water and filter. A-2.2.2 Potassium Iodide Solution - prepared by dissolving 150 g of potassium iodide in water and dilute to 1 litre. Make solution neutral to phenolphthalein. A-2.2.3 Standard Hydrochloric Acid 1 N_ A-2.2.4 Phenolphthalein Indicator Solution

A-2.3 Procedure
A-2.3.1 Complex Formation - Weigh accurately, a sufficient quantity of the sample to contain between 0�1 7 and 0-19 g of dalapon, from a closed weighing bottle into the conical flask with the ground neck. Pipette 100 ml of mercuric nitrate solution into the flask, add some glass beads, attach the condenser and reflux for 15 minutes, after boiling starts. Cool the flask and contents to room temperature. A-2.3.2 Isolation of Complex - Filter off the precipitate with suction using the crucible and a buchner flask. Wash the conical flask and precipitate with water until free from acid. Discard the filtrate and washings. A-2.3.3 Decomposition of tke Complex - Pour 50 ml potassium iodide into the conical flask to dissolve any remaining precipitate. Then add this solution to the precipitate in the crucible and stir until the precipitate dissolves. ( If all the precipitate does not dissolve after 2 minutes then it is to be assumed that the residue is not dalapon-mercury complex.) Apply vacuum
8

IS I 8267 � 1976
and filter the solution containing the dissolved precipitate into a clean buchner flask. Transfer the filtrate to a conical flask, washing the crucible and buchnerflask, with small amounts of potassium iodide. The total volume of the washings shall not exceed 100 ml, Put some glass beads in the flask containing the filtrate, stopper with a bUJ1Sen valve, bring to boil quickly, boiling for one minute only. Cool quickly, under a cold water tap. Titrate immediately, with standard hydrochloric acid using phenolphthalein as an indicator.
NOTE - Carry out a preliminary run to determine the correct proportions of sample and reagent. I t is important to titrate as quickly as possible. If the potassium iodide is allowed to stand for any length of time the titre is reduced.

A-2.4 CaleulatioDS
Dalapon-sodium (uncorrected for sodium 4�499 X v X N pyruvate ), percent by mass c= m where

N

v -= volume in rnl of standard hydrochloric acid used, == normality of the standard hydrochloric acid, and m = mass in g of sample taken for the test.

DETERMINATION OF LOSS ON DRYING p-l. APPARATUS

8-2.1 Phosphorus Pentoxide Desiceant

B-3.PROCEDURE 8-3.1 Put phosphorus pentoxide desiccant in the 10 em petri dish and distribute evenly over the bottom of the dish. Place the dish at the bottom of the desiccator. Dry the 7 em petri dish at 100�0, cool and weigh. Sieve the sample through a 150-micron IS Sieve (see IS: 460�1962� ), and weigh

accurately, about 5 g in the small petri dish. Place the dish on the gauge of the vacuum desiccator. Cover the desiccator, making sure that the seal is effective, and evacuate so that the pressure remains between 5 to 10 mm of mercury during the drying period of 16 h. Release the vacuum, slowly and reweigh the sample and dish.

APPENDIX D [ Table 1, Item (iv) ]
DETERMINATION OF THE COARSE MATERIAL INSOLUBLE IN WATER

0-1. PROCEDURE
D-l.1 Weigh accurately, about 30 g of the sample, mix with 200 ml of water in the stoppered measuring cylinder and shake the mixture for 10 minutes. Pour the solution through a I 50-micron IS Sieve ( IS : 460-1962� ), washing out any residue from the measuring cylinder with water on to the sieve. Wash the residue on the sieve several times with distilled water and allow to drain. Brush the residue remaining on the sieve on a glazed paper and then to the tared weighing bottle. Dry the weighing bottle and residue at IOQoe, cool and reweigh. Calculate the percent by mass of coarse material insoluble in water.
